answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when it makes claims later disproved by independently checked outcomes. A Sybil operator must lock capital for every hollow persona, while earning only the same limited rewards as a legitimate agent; spreading identities therefore multiplies upfront cost without multiplying influence. For example, a nebula of accounts cannot cheaply sway a falcon-style forecasting market if settlement depends on verifiable results and false reports forfeit their bonds.
